note: City of Keokuk riverfront lot at the boat launch on the Mississippi, beside the Southside Boat Club, which holds the restrooms and takes payment. Rail yard and a grain mill next door, so expect noise. Dump is at the city's Bank Street campground. Floods at high water. --Claude
summary: New rate $24 ($20 senior/veteran), 50 amp + water confirmed, count 16->24 on 12 boxes, reservable -> first-come, 7-night max, Memorial Day-Labor Day. Lead riverfront -> riverview.
flags: WATERFRONT LEAD: riverfront -> riverview. Pin ~0 m off Google and is right. NAIP (normal stage): a paved, striped boat-launch lot between Mississippi Drive (north) and the river; ramp and jetty at the south edge. Rail yard and the road are both on the LAND side, so neither lies between the lot and the water. But the lot's drive lane and the public boat launch do: the south rim of pavement is ~20 m through a riprap bank from the Mississippi. That is a driveway and day use between camper and water, so not on-water under the rule. City calls it 'river vista'. I could not place the 12 electric boxes from imagery, so this goes down; if they run on the river rim the view is open. Not a question.
FLOODS: Esri imagery shows the whole lot under brown high water, pin and all (undated). No statement about closure; lot simply floods. Note says so.

PHONE: stored 319-524-4765 is the George M. Verity museum (still listed on the city fee sheet for questions, 9-5). City page says 'For information call 319-524-2050 Ext 2203'; Google agrees; Boat Club 319-524-7122. Should change to 319-524-2050. Stored note's 'reservations via' the museum is wrong and removed: city says no reservations.
WEBSITE: add the city's page https://cityofkeokuk.org/community/public-parks/ (with fee and rules PDFs dated 2024); stored tourism page has a stale 'Sixteen drive-through spaces' and no fee.

RATINGS (city park, not gated): Google 3.2 (21); Campendium camper reports 3.0-4.0, longest rig reported 28 ft; '9/2025 $25' report against the city's $24 and no sign the fee moved. Mill and train noise reported ('large and noisy grain milling plant next door with lots of noise, train traffic'). Criteria: it is a parking lot with pedestals but a real, city-run, posted camping facility. Waste: 'dump station or sewer located at Bank Street', and the city page says 'Bank Street Campground will be closed until further notice due to construction of the riverfront trails project', so the dump may be unavailable; dump left unset.

SEASON CONFLICT WORTH KNOWING: city fee sheet says Memorial Day to Labor Day, its rules say off-season Nov 1-Apr 1 'at some parks'; 1/2015 Campendium camper stayed in winter for the electric. Spring/fall status at this lot is unstated.
